properties.statement:
MEASURED ON THE LIVE GRAPH, AND IT CORRECTS AN EARLIER CLAIM IN THIS SAME CHANGE. Retiring a node type does not merely stop an export CONTAINING that type from importing. It stops EVERY EXISTING GRAPH FROM OPENING AT ALL, instances or no instances, until the graph is migrated.

The reason is that the guard reads the STAMP, not the contents. A graph's stamp records the SCHEMA the writing binary had, so every reflow2 graph in existence names QualityGate whether or not it ever held one. reflow2's own graph held ZERO QualityGate nodes and was refused outright: "this graph names types this reflow2 cannot read, so opening it could silently show you less of your design than it holds — refused."

WHAT I GOT WRONG, AND HOW. I probed the IMPORT path with a hand-built document carrying an undeclared type, saw it refused, and wrote the blast radius from that: "almost certainly affects nobody, since the type never had a constructor and our graph holds zero." The measurement was real and it measured the wrong path. The binding gate is STORE OPEN, which fires on the stamp; instance count never enters it. This is step (5) of the root-cause discipline failing in its documented way — a call that completed, a result that was true, and an inference that did not follow.

THE RETIREMENT IS TWO EDITS, NOT ONE, AND THE CODE SAYS SO. provenance.rs carries RETIRED_NODE_TYPES with the comment "Empty so far; grows the day a node type is retired." Cutting the type from schema/verify.yaml without adding it there left the guard classifying an ordinary graph as one from the FUTURE, so the refusal told the operator their reflow2 was BEHIND and to rebuild — the exact opposite of the correct action. Registering the retirement flips the message to "predates a schema change — migrate the graph", which is right.

THE MIGRATION RECIPE WORKS AND WAS RUN END TO END on the live graph: export with a binary that still knows the type, import into a FRESH graph with the binary that retired it, verify. Result: 3,989 nodes and 21,555 edges in, 3,989 and 21,555 out, zero nodes lost, zero edges lost, stamp 29 → 28.

⚠️ ONE OPERATIONAL TRAP FOUND BY FALLING INTO IT. The stamp lives in a SIDECAR file beside the store, `<graph-path>.meta.json`, not inside the store directory. Copying the store directory into place while leaving the old sidecar reproduces the refusal exactly, on a graph that has already been migrated. Anyone moving a graph by hand must move the sidecar with it; the published recipe avoids this only because importing into a fresh path writes its own.

OPEN AND NOT DECIDED HERE: whether the guard should open the store and COUNT instances before refusing. A retired type with zero instances carries no risk of showing less than the design holds, which is the guard's whole stated purpose — so the refusal is stricter than its own justification requires. Against that: counting means opening the store the guard is refusing to open, and a cheap conservative check is worth more than a clever one. Not this change's call.
